record.paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
record.original_question: Can a variational or related time-propagation method impose positive semidefiniteness on the three-body reduced density matrix Γ(3), and on the resulting one- and two-body reduced density matrices γ and Γ, despite the fact that approximate truncation can break the trace relations connecting these density matrices?

evidence.quote: It is not easy to impose positive-semidefiniteness on Γ (3) and even if it has such property, since its trace relation with γ and Γ is broken this does not lead to the positive-semidefiniteness of γ and Γ.
However, we are exploring variational approaches to impose this constraint during the time evolution, namely preventing the system not to be positive-semidefiniteness.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an N-fermion quantum system with antisymmetric pure or mixed state, and let
- γ denote its one-body reduced density matrix (1-RDM),
- Γ denote its two-body reduced density matrix (2-RDM),
- Γ^(3) denote its three-body reduced density matrix (3-RDM),

obtained by partial traces of the full N-body density operator. Exactly, these objects satisfy contraction (trace) relations
   Tr_3 Γ^(3) = c₂ Γ,    Tr_2 Γ = c₁ γ,
for appropriate combinatorial constants c₁, c₂ depending on N, and each of γ, Γ, Γ^(3) is positive semidefinite.

A truncation of the time-dependent BBGKY-type hierarchy of equations for the reduced density matrices closes the evolution at the level of Γ^(3) by introducing an approximate closure that expresses the four-body RDM in terms of lower-order ones. Such an approximate closure generally breaks the exact trace/contraction relations between Γ^(3), Γ, and γ during time evolution, so that even if Γ^(3)(t) is enforced to be positive semidefinite, the contracted matrices Γ(t) and γ(t) need not remain positive semidefinite.

Problem. Construct a variational (or otherwise constrained) time-propagation scheme for the truncated hierarchy that, throughout the evolution t ≥ 0:
(i) keeps Γ^(3)(t) positive semidefinite, and
(ii) simultaneously guarantees positive semidefiniteness of the resulting one-body and two-body reduced density matrices γ(t) and Γ(t),

despite the fact that the approximate closure breaks the exact contraction relations connecting Γ^(3), Γ, and γ. Equivalently, exhibit a method for imposing these positivity constraints dynamically during time evolution, or prove that no such scheme can simultaneously satisfy (i) and (ii) under a generic closure that violates the contraction identities.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search shows extensive literature on variational determination of ground-state 2-RDMs via semidefinite programming with N-representability/positive semidefiniteness constraints, but no established time-dependent scheme that simultaneously enforces positive semidefiniteness of Γ^(3) and of the contracted γ, Γ when the truncation breaks the contraction relations. The question of designing such a constrained time-propagation scheme appears to remain an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Variational calculations of fermion second-order reduced density matrices by semidefinite programming algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: Ground-state 2-RDM determined variationally using P, Q, G positive-semidefiniteness conditions as necessary N-representability constraints.
status_evidence.claim: Existing variational/SDP methods enforce positive semidefiniteness only in the static (ground-state) setting, not along time evolution under a truncated BBGKY-type hierarchy.

status_evidence.title: Variational reduced-density-matrix method using three-particle N-representability conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Three-index T1, T2 N-representability conditions imposed via standard semidefinite programming for ground states.
status_evidence.claim: Three-particle positivity conditions are studied for static variational RDM theory; no time-dependent analogue addressing broken contraction relations is reported.

status_evidence.title: Determining the N-Representability of a Reduced Density Matrix via Unitary Evolution and Stochastic Sampling
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work probing N-representability via unitary evolution and stochastic sampling.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research suggests the dynamical-positivity problem for truncated RDM hierarchies is not yet considered solved.
